reception: The citing literature received the work mostly as a marker. Its main afterlife is in surveys of reconfigurable computing — Compton and Hauck, Todman and colleagues, Tessier and Burleson — where the compiler stands as an example of carrying sequential C and Fortran all the way to hardware. Engaged citations are few: the DIVA processing-in-memory work differentiates its architecture against this approach, and Rugina and Rinard's pointer analysis for structured parallel programs made use of the compiler. Most other citations name the paper in passing while mapping the space of C-to-gates compilation, so the reception is modest in depth if not in venue.
